text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today, closing at $389.68, after climbing sharply through mid-September. The immediate trigger appears to be geopolitical uncertainty around Iran: while diplomatic talks at the UN offered hope for de-escalation and potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Wall Street analysts openly admitted they don't know how the situation will resolve or what oil prices will do next. That uncertainty spooked investors in a refiner that profits from the spread between crude costs and refined product prices.

Adding to the pressure is a potential policy headwind—the Trump administration is examining a diesel export ban to address high fuel costs for farmers and truckers. A ban would restrict Marathon's ability to sell diesel overseas at premium prices, directly hitting refinery margins. With refineries already running at high capacity (96.8%) and storage levels elevated, the company faces both geopolitical fog and the risk of tighter domestic fuel policy.
